articles.title: .NET MAUI 11 Makes CoreCLR the Default Runtime and Adds Incremental XAML Hot Reload
articles.summary: Microsoft released .NET 11 with a .NET MAUI update focused on product quality. CoreCLR is now the default runtime on all platforms, and XAML gets incremental hot reload, implicit namespaces and faster resource dictionaries. The release also adds device test templates and passkey support, and raises the minimum Android and Apple platform versions. By Edin Kapić

articles.title: Teaching AI About Disordered Proteins? I’d Start at 50 Milliseconds
articles.summary:
If AlphaFold gives you 25 different pictures of two proteins bound together, which one would you trust enough to plan an experiment around?

A LinkedIn post about AlphaFold and disordered proteins got me thinking about that question from the lab’s side. I think there’s a specific gap we can fill with FastHDX. We can measure which stretches of a disordered protein change when a partner binds, including changes that are visible only in the first fraction of a second of labelling. articles.title: What goes into a LoRA recipe for Spark-X2.5?
articles.summary:
You have a Spark-X2.5 checkpoint and a training dataset. Where do you start? Surogate's v1.5.16 release gives you a small BF16 LoRA recipe whose settings you can inspect before launching a run.



The example points to Spark-X2.5-1.7B. It uses a LoRA rank of 16, alpha 32, a sequence length of 1,024, and a cap of 100 training steps. These are settings in the example. The guide shows how to switch to Spark-X2.5-4B, with batch size and sequence length adjustable for your GPU. Start with the v1.5.16 YAML and the training guide.

articles.title: CORS blocked? Your browser is protecting you — your API call took the wrong road
articles.summary:
You asked your AI to wire up an API. It wrote a fetch call, hit run, and the console says:


Access to fetch at 'https://api.example.com/data' has been blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present.


Nothing is wrong with your fetch code. This is the browser doing its job.

What CORS actually is

Your page lives on one domain. The API lives on another. The browser asks the API, "Do you allow calls from this page?" If the API doesn't answer yes, the browser refuses — before the API ever sees the request. It's a permission handshake, not a bug in your app.

articles.title: Mock Service Worker Releases v3.0 with ESM-Only Build, Socket-Based Interception and GraphQL Subs
articles.summary: Mock Service Worker 3.0 is now ESM-only, requires Node.js 22 or later, and cuts package size from 416KB to 234KB. It adds GraphQL subscription support, protocol-specific entrypoints, and an experimental defineNetwork API. Node.js interception now works at the TCP and TLS level. Some users report test failures from newly intercepted OPTIONS preflight requests. By Daniel Curtis

articles.title: Shuffle the Questions to Catch an LLM That Memorized Its Benchmark
articles.summary:
Two short Python functions and a free Colab GPU score a model in about half an hour; a z above 3 merits a look, while a near-zero score is more of a shrug.
The post Shuffle the Questions to Catch an LLM That Memorized Its Benchmark appeared first on Towards Data Science.

articles.title: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
articles.summary: OpenAI will introduce a single usage meter across ChatGPT as it combines the Chat and Work experiences.

articles.title: Vercel Launched Experimental Board to Coordinate Tasks Across Humans and Coding Agents
articles.summary: Vercel's experimental Board is a headless message store where people and coding agents claim leased tasks, declare dependencies, and sync threads with Slack, GitHub, and Linear. By Daniel Dominguez

articles.title: DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2.5 Aims to Make Robots Safer, More Dexterous, and Faster Learners
articles.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, a vision-language-action (VLA) model designed to improve robots' dexterity, reliability, and learning speed, while enabling safer operation in unstructured real-world environments. By Sergio De Simone

articles.title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York
articles.summary: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years as new research from Common Sense Media reveals troubling safety failures, including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to emotional development.

articles.title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15
articles.summary: AWS has raised the maximum timeout of on-demand Lambda Event Functions from 15 to 30 minutes in all commercial regions, with no opt-in and no new pricing. The limit had stood since 2018. AWS's post lists the costs: twice the concurrency at the same request rate, three-hour SQS visibility timeouts, and Kafka mappings that must be recreated. Practitioners welcome it and ask what belongs elsewhere. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

articles.title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts
articles.summary: Rust 1.100.0, released 12 November 2026, stabilises the never type (!) after ten years of work and makes Infallible an alias for it. The release also stabilises the core of the allocator API, adds DropGuard, and gives Cargo an opt-in dependency cooldown setting. Some critics note the allocator design still lacks inline storage support. By Daniel Curtis
